rows.name: World 1-1 first screen (overworld, level start)
rows.notes: First playable screen of World 1-1: fixed HUD (MARIO/score, coin icon x00, WORLD 1-1, TIME 393), periwinkle sky, one small cloud, a green hill on the left (small Mario standing on it), one bush on the right, and the brick ground row filling the bottom 4 tile rows. BACKGROUND PATTERN TABLE: $1000 - every nametable tile id $00-$FF is drawn from CHR $100-$1FF (verified: nametable tile $B4 reads CHR $1B4, tile $34 reads CHR $134). WHICH BG PALETTE PAINTS WHAT (live palette RAM confirmed): palette 0 = [$22 periwinkle, $29 lime green, $1A green, $0F black] paints the HILL (slot 2 $1A green + slot 3 $0F black outline, get_region at (25,196) returned slots 2,3) and the BUSH (slot 1 $29 lime green body + slot 2 $1A shading + slot 3 $0F outline, get_region at (215,200) returned slots 1,2,3); slot 0 $22 is the shared backdrop/sky. Palette 1 = [$0F, $36 peach, $17 brown, $0F] paints the GROUND/BRICK row (get_region at (10,228) returned slots 1,2,3; rendered highlight sampled $36 peach at (10,226)). Palette 2 = [$0F, $30 white, $21 sky blue, $0F] paints the cloud. Palette 3 = [$0F, $27 orange, $17 brown, $0F] paints the ? block (none on this first screen). Scroll is 0 and the HUD occupies the top 4 tile rows (y 0-31).
rows.why: the screenshot is World 1-1's first screen as named: HUD WORLD 1-1, hill left, bush right, cloud, ground rows; BG table $1000 and palette roles (palette 0 hill/bush, 1 ground) agree with the picture

rows.name: small Mario (standing/right, 2x2 metasprite in a 2x4 box)
rows.notes: World 1-1, small (not Super) Mario. The game emits him as 8 OAM entries in a 2-wide x 4-tall box (16x32) but only the lower two rows are real; the top two rows are four transparent $FC padding tiles. Palette 4 for every entry. Offsets are tile-column/tile-row from the box top-left, which sat at screen (40,177) in this frame. OAM#1 tile $FC @ (0,0) no flip - blank padding. OAM#2 $FC @ (8,0) no flip - blank. OAM#3 $FC @ (0,8) no flip - blank. OAM#4 $FC @ (8,8) no flip - blank. OAM#5 $3A @ (0,16) no flip - head left half (hat/hair/face). OAM#6 $37 @ (8,16) no flip - head right half. OAM#7 $4F @ (0,24) no flip - body left. OAM#8 $4F @ (8,24) H-FLIPPED - body right (the only flipped tile). Proof: pause_emulator then list_sprites hit-tested at Mario pixel (44,204) returned exactly one sprite, OAM#7 chr_tile 79 ($4F), palette 4, flip_h false, pixel_value 2; a second list_sprites over the whole frame returned the 8 entries above all at palette 4 with tiles FC,FC,FC,FC,3A,37,4F,4F and flips none/none/none/none/none/none/none/h. Facing right in this frame (SMB stores the left pose as separate tiles and h-flips them).
rows.why: OAM tiles $3A/$37 (head, cap and face) over $4F and $4F h-flipped (legs), four $FC padding entries above; rendered from sprite CHR they are small Mario standing, as drawn at (40,193) in the screenshot

rows.name: small Mario sprite palette (red cap/shirt, skin, olive hair+shoes)
rows.notes: Sprite palette 4, the one small Mario is painted with; get_palette 4 = [34, 22, 39, 24] = $22, $16, $27, $18. What each slot paints: slot 0 = $22 periwinkle - never visible on Mario (sprite pixel value 0 is transparent; the four real tiles use only indices 1,2,3). slot 1 = $16 red - the cap and the shirt/overalls (all the solid red of the sprite). slot 2 = $27 orange - the face/skin and the hands. slot 3 = $18 olive - hair, sideburns, the dark outline and the shoes. Proof (one-slot experiment): while paused I wrote slot 1 = $2C cyan with write_palette (frozen), stepped one frame and screenshotted - the cap and the whole body turned cyan (get_pixel_color (48,193) and (45,193) = $2C cyan, both pixels are tile $37/$3A index 1), while the face pixel (50,195) stayed $27 orange and the hair/eye pixel (49,195) stayed $18 olive. clear_palette_overrides restored $16 red. Blast radius: any other sprite drawn with palette 4 changes too.
rows.why: after slot 1 was written cyan, Mario's cap and body are cyan in the screenshot while face and hair keep their colors; slot 1 red = cap/body, 2 skin, 3 hair and shoes, as claimed

rows.name: brick top-left (same tile is also the top-right quadrant of the block)
rows.notes: CHR $145 (BG pattern table $1000, nametable tile id $45), top 8x8 row of the 16x16 breakable brick block in World 1-1. Pixel grid: row0 all index 1 (the block's top highlight), rows1-2 index 2 with index 3 at col7, row3 all index 3 (horizontal mortar), rows4-6 index 2 with index 3 at col3, row7 all index 3 - i.e. a brick texture designed to repeat horizontally. Placed in the live nametable twice: rows 18 cols 16 AND 17 both hold $45 (PPU $2650,$2651 = 45 45), so this one tile is both the top-left and the top-right quadrant of the block. Palette 1 (slot 1 $36 peach highlight, slot 2 $17 brown face, slot 3 $0F black mortar). Proof: get_region object mode at (232,152) returned 256 connected background palette-1 pixels, box (231,144)-(246,159), CHR 0x145/0x147; get_tile_at_pixel (233,148) and (241,148) both returned tile_id 69 ($45) / chr_tile 325; read_memory ppu 9808 len 2 = [69,69] and read_nametable 1 (16,18) = 45 45.
rows.why: CHR $145/$147 are the brick texture (top row highlight, mortar lines), each used twice across the block; the breakable bricks in the screenshot's row at y=144-159

rows.name: Title screen (SUPER MARIO BROS. logo + 1/2 PLAYER menu)
rows.notes: Everything on this screen is background: nametable 0, BG PATTERN TABLE $1000 (nametable tile ids $00-$FF draw CHR $100-$1FF). It shows the 'SUPER MARIO BROS.' sign, a '(c)1985 NINTENDO' line, and the '1 PLAYER GAME / 2 PLAYER GAME' menu with the mushroom cursor, over the World 1-1 backdrop (hill/bush/ground) plus the fixed top HUD. Start begins a game; Start during the attract demo only returns to the title.
rows.why: the screenshot taken before any press is the title screen: SUPER MARIO BROS. sign, (c)1985 NINTENDO, 1/2 PLAYER GAME menu, TOP- 000000, over the 1-1 backdrop

rows.name: Title logo: 'SUPER MARIO BROS.' sign
rows.notes: THE PROOF: get_region object mode at (60,70) returned one connected background object, palette 1, slots 1,2,3, 3328 pixels, box (40,38)-(91,101) (truncated - continues beyond the 64x64 window), CHR tiles $126,$142,$143,$144,$146,$148 and 15 more incl. $1D0-$1E8. TILE RANGE: the sign board/frame uses nametable tile ids $26 and $38 (solid fills) plus $42-$4A (top/side border, corners); the 'SUPER MARIO BROS.' letterforms use nametable tile ids $D0-$E8. PATTERN TABLE: all from the BG pattern table $1000 (CHR $100-$1FF), e.g. tile $D7 at screen (56,64) reads CHR $1D7, and tile $48 (border) reads CHR $148. Palette 1 paints slot 1 $36 peach (letters), slot 2 $17 brown (board), slot 3 $0F black (outline).
rows.why: the sign in the screenshot; CHR $1D0-$1E8 render as big-letter curve and stroke parts and $142-$14A as the board's edges and riveted corners, from table $1000, palette 1 peach/brown/black; one slip: $38 is a bush edge, not a board fill

rows.name: Status bar layout (MARIO / score / coins / WORLD / TIME)
rows.notes: Fixed top 4 tile rows of nametable 0 (rows 0-3, screen y 0-31), BG pattern table $1000, all text BG palette 2 ($30 white) except the coin icon (palette 3). ROW 2 (y 16-23) = LABELS: 'MARIO' = tiles $16,$0A,$1B,$12,$18 at cols 3-7; 'WORLD' = $20,$18,$1B,$15,$0D at cols 18-22; 'TIME' = $1D,$12,$16,$0E at cols 25-28. ROW 3 (y 24-31) = VALUES: score = six digit tiles ($00...) at cols 3-8; coin icon $2E at col 11, 'x' $29 at col 12, coin-count digits at cols 13-14; world/level number '1-1' = $01,$28,$01 at cols 19-21; TIME value = three digits at cols 26-28. PROOF: read_nametable(0,0) 32x4 compared with the screenshot - on the title screen the TIME value cells (row 3 cols 26-28) are blank sky $24, matching the screenshot's 'TIME' with no number; after Start, wait, Start into World 1-1 the same cells read $03,$09,$08 = '398', matching the in-game screenshot's TIME 398 while score/coin/world cells stayed as read.
rows.why: the screenshot's labels sit where claimed: MARIO from x=24 (col 3), WORLD x=144 (col 18), TIME x=200 (col 25) on row 2; score col 3-8, coin icon col 11, 1-1 cols 19-21 and TIME 398 cols 26-28 on row 3
